health.title: Financial health
health.description: A score out of 100 from four simple, documented rules. Each factor is worth 25 points.
health.welcomeBody: Here is your starting health score. Try the what-if simulator to see how small changes move it.
health.basisHistory_one: Based on your last complete month.
health.basisHistory_other: Based on your last {{count}} complete months.
health.basisPlan: Based on your plan, until you have a full month of activity.

overall.fair: On the way. A couple of factors need attention.
overall.poor: Needs attention. Start with the lowest factor.

health.tipAi: Suggestion written by AI from your numbers

savingsRate.title: Savings rate
savingsRate.definition: Income left after spending, as a share of income

emergencyFund.title: Emergency fund
emergencyFund.definition: Months of essential spending your emergency fund covers

debtToIncome.title: Debt to income
debtToIncome.definition: Minimum debt payments as a share of income

fixedCosts.title: Fixed costs
fixedCosts.definition: Bills you pay no matter what, as a share of income

savingsRate.good: You keep a healthy share of your income. Point it at your top goal so it has a job.
savingsRate.fair: You are saving something. Try moving one small, regular expense into savings each month.
savingsRate.poor: Spending is close to or above income. Look at your two biggest flexible categories first.
savingsRate.unknown: Add your income to see your savings rate.

emergencyFund.good: Your cushion covers six months or more. New savings can go to goals.
emergencyFund.fair: You have a start. Building towards three, then six months, makes surprises much less stressful.
emergencyFund.poor: A small emergency fund first, even one month of essentials, protects every other plan.
emergencyFund.unknown: Add your essential costs or an emergency fund to see this.

debtToIncome.good: Your debt payments are a small part of income. Keep paying more than the minimum when you can.
debtToIncome.fair: Debt payments take a noticeable share. Compare avalanche and snowball to clear them faster.
debtToIncome.poor: Debt payments take a large share of income. Focus extra money on one debt at a time.
debtToIncome.unknown: Add your income to see this.

fixedCosts.good: Your fixed costs leave plenty of room each month.
fixedCosts.fair: Fixed costs take a big share. Review subscriptions and bills for anything you no longer use.
fixedCosts.poor: Fixed costs leave little room. Even one renegotiated bill makes a lasting difference.
fixedCosts.unknown: Add your income to see this.

health.rulesNote: How each factor is calculated is documented in the project's finance rules. The AI only writes suggestions; it never computes the score.
